problem: Agentic LLM augmentation for autonomous navigation is usually run on cloud compute, so its real-time feasibility on the constrained hardware of embodied robots is unknown. Prior work does not compare augmentation methods (ReMEmbR vs CAG) across embedded and consumer hardware.
motivation: Embodied robots must answer spatial and position queries on-board and in real time, under limited compute and memory. The paper compares an embedded AI computer (Jetson Orin AGX) with consumer-grade hardware, and compares two memory augmentation methods, on both latency and accuracy.
key_idea: Benchmark ReMEmbR (retrieval-augmented memory) against Cache Augmented Generation for spatial queries on a Jetson Orin AGX and on consumer GPUs, to test real-time feasibility and accuracy.
insight: On the Jetson Orin AGX, position-related queries could not be answered in real time. On consumer hardware, larger models with CAG appeared to give higher precision. Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited.
method: ReMEmbR: retrieval-augmented memory for embodied robots, used to answer spatial queries.
CAG (Cache Augmented Generation): the memory is preloaded into the LLM context/KV cache, the alternative augmentation method.
Hardware comparison: Jetson Orin AGX embedded computer vs consumer-grade hardware, evaluating real-time feasibility.
Accuracy evaluation: multiple LLMs of different parameter counts are compared on spatial (position) queries under both augmentation methods.

setting.backbone: multiple LLMs (unspecified in abstract), likely frozen
setting.observation: robot memory of past observations/positions (details not given in abstract)
setting.action_space: not specified (spatial question answering for navigation)

results: The Jetson Orin AGX could not achieve real-time performance for position-related queries. On consumer hardware, models with more parameters seemed to improve precision when using CAG. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
limitations: Only qualitative findings are available; the evaluation scope and query set are unclear.
Real-time feasibility was tested only on one embedded platform (Jetson Orin AGX).
No standard navigation benchmark is reported.
compares_to: Jetson Orin AGX vs consumer-grade hardware
